water between them heaves and knots. Tall, smooth-backed swells pass
beneath you without breaking. The clouds hang so low that they seem to
brush the wave tops. Your boat climbs and drops with a slow, queasy
rhythm.

9526.name: At cross-currents in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies In the ocean.

east.description: To the east lies At a bend in the current.

south.description: To the south lies At a cross-currents.

9526.description:
Currents from the north, east and south crash together here, heaping the
water into steep, pointed waves that collapse as fast as they rise. The
water has a strange chill to it, and the light has turned flat and grey.
Somewhere beyond the haze a deep, slow tolling rolls across the water.
Your boat pitches wildly, shipping spray at every plunge.

9527.name: In the ocean

south.description: To the south lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

west.description: To the west lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

9527.description:
Grey haze lies over the ocean here, softening the horizon and muffling
every sound. The swell is long and low, and the water has a cold, leaden
look. One current slides away south toward churning water, and another
runs west. Drops of mist gather on your sleeves and run together.

9528.name: At a cross-currents

north.description: To the north lies In the ocean.

east.description: To the east lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

west.description: To the west lies At a sharp turn in the current.

9528.description:
Here the currents collide in a broad, seething patch, and ridges of
white water run across it like ploughed furrows. Your boat is tossed
from one ridge to the next, its timbers groaning. Calmer streams lead
away north, east and west. The noise of the churning water drowns out
even the wind.

9529.name: In the ocean

south.description: To the south lies At a cross-currents.

west.description: To the west lies At a bend in the current.

9529.description:
Open ocean surrounds you here, empty and blue to the rim of the world. A
light breeze ruffles the water into tiny wavelets that glitter like
scattered glass. The current runs south toward a patch of troubled water
and west toward a quiet, weed-strewn bend. Your boat's shadow slides
along beneath you on the clear water.

9530.name: At cross-currents in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies At a sharp turn in the current.

south.description: To the south lies At a bend in the current.

west.description: To the west lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

9530.description:
The ocean here is crossed by a tangle of currents, its surface a
patchwork of glassy slicks and broken water. Your boat glides across a
smooth patch, then bucks as it strikes a band of chop. One stream sets
north toward a sharp turn, another curves away south, and a third runs
back west. Far off, the sun glints on something white at the edge of the
world.

9531.name: At a north-south current in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

south.description: To the south lies At a bend in the current.

9531.description:
The current flows north and south here, strong and smooth, between two
long ridges of standing waves. Your boat runs along the channel between
them like a cartwheel in a rut. Beyond the ridges the sea is broken and
wild, while inside them the water is almost glassy. Spray from the
standing waves drifts over you in a fine, cool mist.

9532.name: At cross-currents in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

south.description: To the south lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

west.description: To the west lies At a cross-currents.

9532.description:
Here a current running north and south crosses another that flows in
from the west, and the water turns in a slow, broad eddy. At its heart a
dimple of spinning water sucks in flecks of foam. Your boat circles
once, then twice, before you can pull clear. The sky above is a pale,
washed blue.

9533.name: At a north-south current in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies In the ocean.

south.description: To the south lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

9533.description:
A narrow current runs north and south here, a ribbon of darker blue laid
across the paler sea. On either side the water lies still and bright,
flashing back the sun. A faint smell of rain rides the breeze from the
north. Your boat settles into the stream as if it knows the way.

9534.name: In the ocean

south.description: To the south lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

west.description: To the west lies In the ocean.

9534.description:
The ocean here turns in a lazy circle, and rowing west only brings you
round to the same patch of water. A small squall passes overhead,
pattering on the sea and freshening the air. Rainwater gathers in the
bottom of your boat. Only the current running south seems to lead
anywhere.

9535.name: At cross-currents in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

east.description: To the east lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

south.description: To the south lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

9535.description:
Currents from three directions collide here, churning the water into a
mess of peaked, slapping waves. A slow whirl of foam turns in the middle
of it all. The northern stream leads toward a green island, the southern
back toward a walled harbour, and an eastern branch slides off into open
sea. Spray rattles against the hull like thrown gravel.

9536.name: At a bend in the current

north.description: To the north lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

west.description: To the west lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

9536.description:
The current sweeps from north to west here in a wide, curving bend. On
the outside of the curve the water runs fast and ruffled, while on the
inside it lies smooth and dark. Far off, a bank of grey cloud sits low
upon the sea. A cool wind blows across the bend and raises gooseflesh on
your arms.

9537.name: At a sharp turn in the current

east.description: To the east lies At a bend in the current.

south.description: To the south lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

9537.description:
The current turns hard here, almost doubling back on itself, and your
boat is flung round so sharply that you must grab the gunwale. Water
mounds on the outside of the bend in a smooth, glassy hump. The stream
arriving from the south swings away east. A faint mist hangs over the
turn, cool and salty on your face.

9538.name: At a bend in the current

north.description: To the north lies At a sharp turn in the current.

west.description: To the west lies At a sharp turn in the current.

9538.description:
The current bends gently here, curving from west to north in a long,
lazy arc. The water is calmer than at the sharp turn, and you can rest
your arms a while. Far to the north a smudge of land lies along the
horizon, half lost in haze. Sunlight dapples the swell in shifting coins
of gold.

9539.name: At the harbor to Timeless Island

north.description: To the north lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

south.description: To the south lies At the harbor to Timeless Island.

9539.description:
The harbor to Timeless Island opens before you, its quays of pale gold
stone glowing in a light that seems to come from nowhere. Yet however
hard you row south toward them, the current curls gently round and sets
you back where you began. The air is warm and utterly still, and the
water holds the sky like a mirror. Only the way north, back through the
channel, leads anywhere at all.

extra_descs.quays quay gold:
Beyond the quays rise white towers and terraces, and on the tallest
stands a great clock whose hands do not move. The longer you look at it,
the less sure you are of how long you have been looking.

9540.name: At a north-south current in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies At the entrance to a harbor.

south.description: To the south lies At the harbor to Timeless Island.

9540.description:
The current runs north and south here through the channel between the
two moles. The water is eerily still, and your boat slides over it
without a ripple or a sound. Strangely, no weed or barnacle clings to
the stones of the moles, which look as fresh as the day they were laid.
South lies the harbor to Timeless Island, wrapped in a golden haze.

9541.name: At a sharp turn in the current

east.description: To the east lies At the entrance to a harbor.

south.description: To the south lies At a bend in the current.

9541.description:
The current arriving from the south snaps round a sharp corner here and
races off east. In that direction two long stone moles reach out into
the sea, marking the entrance to a harbour. The water is quick and
ruffled, and your boat skips over it like a flat stone. A smell of
woodsmoke drifts out across the water.

9542.name: At the entrance to a harbor

south.description: To the south lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

west.description: To the west lies At a sharp turn in the current.

9542.description:
Two long moles of tumbled stone reach out into the ocean here, and
between them the current flows south into a quiet harbour channel. A
white lighthouse stands at the tip of one mole, its lamp burning with a
pale, steady glow that never flickers. Beyond the moles the water is
flat and still as glass. Back west, the current races round its sharp
turn.

9543.name: At a north-south current in the ocean

north.description: To the north lies Going around an island.

south.description: To the south lies At cross-currents in the ocean.

9543.description:
The current runs swiftly north here toward a wooded island whose cliffs
rise sheer from the sea. Its pull is so strong that rowing back south
toward the cross-currents is hard, sweaty work. The cliffs are streaked
white by generations of nesting birds. The water darkens as it runs into
the island's shadow.

9544.name: Going around an island

south.description: To the south lies At a north-south current in the ocean.

west.description: To the west lies Going around an island.

9544.description:
Here the current, arriving from the south, curls along the foot of the
island's cliffs and bends away west. Sea caves gape in the rock just
above the waterline, too narrow for a boat, and boom like drums as the
swell surges into them. The island towers over you, its crown dark with
pines. Cold spray drifts from the cliff foot and beads on your skin.

9545.name: Going around an island

north.description: To the north lies Going around an island.

east.description: To the east lies Going around an island.

9545.description:
The current hugs the island here, sweeping your boat past a narrow strip
of grey shingle hemmed in by cliffs. Each wave rattles the pebbles as it
drains back, a sound like a long indrawn breath. The current is too
strong to let you land, and bears you on around the shore. The island
curves away north, and the sea caves lie back to the east.

9546.name: Going around an island

east.description: To the east lies Going around an island.

south.description: To the south lies Going around an island.

9546.description:
On this side of the island the cliffs give way to steep slopes of grass
and wildflowers that tumble to the water's edge. A roofless stone hut
stands on a ledge above the shore, its doorway staring out to sea. The
scent of thyme drifts out over the water. The current swings east along
the shore from here, and south back toward the shingle beach.

9547.name: Going around an island

east.description: To the east lies Going around an island.

west.description: To the west lies Going around an island.

9547.description:
The current runs fast and straight here, squeezed between the island and
a line of half-sunken rocks. White water foams over the rocks with every
swell, and your boat shoots along the channel like an arrow. On the
island a stream falls from the hillside in a silver thread and spills
into the sea. The channel runs on east and back west.

9548.name: Going around an island

south.description: To the south lies In front of an island pier.

west.description: To the west lies Going around an island.

9548.description:
The current rounds the last point of the island here and turns south
toward a long wooden pier. A tall stone pillar stands on the point,
carved with weathered spirals and crowned by a bronze dish gone green
with age. Gentle swells lap at the foot of the pillar. The narrow
channel between the rocks lies back to the west.

extra_descs.pillar spirals dish:
The spirals wind inward to a single carved eye at the heart of the
stone. The bronze dish on top is blackened inside, as though fires were
once lit there to guide boats around the point.

9549.name: In front of an island pier

north.description: To the north lies Going around an island.

west.description: To the west lies The Road To Eden.

9549.description:
To the west a long pier of silvered timber runs out from the island, and
beyond it a road winds away between flowering trees. A tall gate of iron
bars closes the landward end of the pier, so thickly grown with vines
and white blossom that it cannot have opened in years. A sweet scent
drifts across the water from the gardens beyond. The current runs back
north around the point.

extra_descs.gate vines blossom:
The bars of the gate are wrought into leaves and hanging fruit, and a
heavy lock rusted solid holds it shut. Through the vines you glimpse a
road of pale stone climbing into a green and sunlit country.

12001.name: The Chief's Office

down.description: There is a rickety ladder leading down.

12001.description:
The guild chief's office is a cramped loft under the warehouse roof,
reached only by the trapdoor in its floor. Its walls are covered with
slates on which the results of every bout and race are chalked in
columns, alongside odds, wagers and debts owed. A small round window
looks out over the fighting ground far below. A strongbox is bolted to
the floor beside a battered desk, and the trapdoor leads down to the
guild office.

12002.name: The Guild Office

up.description: You see a rickety ladder with a trapdoor leading up.

down.description: There is a marble staircase leading down.

12002.description:
The guild that runs the games in the warehouse keeps its office in this
narrow room above the benches, behind a screen of carved lattice through
which the crowd can be watched unseen. A sloping desk holds the guild's
great ledger, and the walls are hung with painted bills announcing bouts
and races. A ladder climbs up to a trapdoor in the ceiling, and a steep
stair leads down to the seating below. The muffled roar of the crowd
rises through the floor.

12003.name: The Southwest Corner Of The Main Warehouse
12003.description:
The main warehouse of Port Halyon is built around an open yard, and here
two towering walls of salt-stained stone meet in a corner under the grey
sky. Bales and barrels stand stacked in roped tiers against the
stonework, and the cobbles are slick with spilled oil. A timber stair
climbs up the wall to the Guild Office, and worn steps lead down into
the basement. A door in the south wall opens on the porters' kitchen,
while the yard runs on north and east between more stacks of cargo.

north.description: To the north lies The Northwest Corner Of The Warehouse.

east.description: To the east lies The Southwest Corner Of The Warehouse.

south.description: You see a small hallway that leads to a larger area.

up.description: Watch your step!

down.description: Watch your step!

12004.name: The Small Kitchen

north.description: The tunnel looks like it leads to another seating area.

east.description: There is an acrid smell coming from that direction.

12004.description:
This small kitchen is little more than a soot-blackened roof on posts,
built against the outer wall of the main warehouse to feed the porters.
A brick hearth with an iron spit fills one side, and a long trestle
table scarred by knives stands before it. Smoke curls out from under the
eaves into the grey sky. The warehouse door lies to the north, and a
path leads east to the First-Aid Station.

212005.name: The West Gate

east.description: To the east lies River Avenue.

west.description: To the west lies The Great Eastern Desert.

212005.description:
Two squat towers of sun-bleached stone flank the West Gate, their arrow
slits facing out over the dunes. Sand blows through the open gateway and
drifts in ridges against the inner wall, where nobody has troubled to
sweep it. West of the arch the paving ends and the Great Eastern Desert
begins, shimmering in the heat. East of the gate, River Avenue leads
into Port Halyon, smelling of mud, tar and the sea.

212006.name: The Weapons Shop

north.description: To the north lies River Avenue.

west.description: To the west lies The Back Room.

212006.description:
Blades of every kind cover the walls of this shop, hung on pegs in fans
and rows: cutlasses, boarding axes, long knives and heavy sabres, all
oiled and gleaming. A long counter of scarred oak stands before a
grindstone, and the smell of oil and hot steel hangs in the air. A door
in the west wall leads into the back room, where the stock is kept. The
street door opens north onto River Avenue.

12007.name: The Back Room
12007.description:
This cramped back room of the Weapons Shop is a storeroom packed almost
to the ceiling with crates of blades and armour, many still stencilled
with the marks of foundries along the coast. Racks of spears lean
against the walls, and a grindstone on a wooden frame stands in the one
clear corner beside a bench stained dark with oil. No window lets in the
light, and the air smells of iron, grease and sawdust. The only way out
is the door back east into the shop.

east.description: To the east lies The Weapons Shop.

12008.name: The Supervisor's Office

down.description: Watch your step!

12008.description:
The supervisor of the warehouse keeps his office here in the open air,
on a platform built out from the roof above the galleries and shaded by
a canvas awning that snaps in the sea wind. A heavy table is bolted to
the planks, and a speaking trumpet of brass hangs on a hook beside it.
From the rail you can see the whole sunken yard spread below, and beyond
the roofs the masts of the harbour. A stair leads down into the
galleries.

12009.name: The Northwest Corner Of The Basement

east.description: There is a large oval dirt-track in that direction.

south.description: To the south lies The Southwest Corner Of The Basement.

12009.description:
The basement of the main warehouse is no cellar but a vast sunken yard,
open to the sky, with the warehouse's galleries rising in tiers of
timber and stone on every side. This corner of the yard is given over to
practice: wooden posts hacked to splinters, straw dummies on poles and a
rack of blunted spears chained to the wall. The ground is a mix of
trampled grass and sand. The yard stretches east along the track and
south toward the far corner.

12010.name: The Southwest Corner Of The Basement
12010.description:
The warehouse basement was dug deep into the riverbank, and in this
corner its vaulted roof gave way long ago, leaving a sunken yard open to
the sky between walls of mossy stone. Coarse grass has taken the silt
floor, worn bare in a broad ring of raked sand where a battered wooden
post stands, hacked and splintered by practice blows. The yard runs on
north toward the rest of the drill ground, and east the vaults still
hold over a darker stretch of the basement. Steps cut into the wall
climb up to the main warehouse.

north.description: Through a small tunnel you can see athletes stretching and warming up for the games.

east.description: To the east lies The Southeast Corner Of The Basement.

up.description: You see a set of steps leading up into the spectator stands.

12011.name: The First-Aid Station

east.description: The South Entrance To The Coliseum

west.description: The cobblestones lead to The Southern Commoner's Seats

12011.description:
A canvas awning stretched between two posts shelters a pair of narrow
cots and a scrubbed table, and that is the whole of the first-aid
station. Strips of linen hang drying on a line, and a water butt stands
by one post with a dipper chained to its rim. The sharp smell of vinegar
and lye cannot quite cover the older smell of blood. Porters hurt by
falling cargo are carried here from the river dock to the east, and the
kitchen lies a few steps west.

12005.name: On The Canal
12005.description:
The canal begins here, its green water let in from the river through a
channel lined with dressed stone. A cobbled towpath runs along the quay,
and an old iron gate stands in the town wall beside it, rusted fast and
laced with creepers that have grown through its bars for years. Through
them you glimpse barren, sun-scorched country stretching away toward the
desert. The towpath follows the canal east into the town, and a stone
stair leads south down to the covered boathouse on the river.

east.description: Through the clouds of dust, you can make out a passable road.

south.description: You can barely make out a storefront through the foliage.

12012.name: On The Canal

east.description: Through the dust, you see a paved road.

west.description: It is difficult to see through the haze and dust.

12012.description:
A towpath of beaten earth runs beside the canal here, its grassy verge
trodden bare by the horses that haul barges toward the docks. The green
canal water lies still and deep between its stone walls, flecked with
chaff. Eastward the path leads to the warehouse dock, and westward it
runs toward an old gate at the edge of the town. Elder bushes grow along
the bank, grey with dust.

12015.name: The Northwest Corner Of The Warehouse
12015.description:
A broad roof of heavy beams covers this corner of the warehouse, and the
shade beneath it is cool and dim after the open yard. Sacks of grain and
bolts of sailcloth are piled high on raised pallets to keep them off the
damp flagstones, and the low ceiling is hung with hooks and pulley
blocks. A narrow wooden stair climbs up to the Supervisor's Office. The
covered bay opens east onto more of the warehouse, and south into the
yard.

east.description: Rows upon rows of bleachers lie to the east.

south.description: To the south lies The Southwest Corner Of The Main Warehouse.

up.description: The stairs look safe enough.

12016.name: The Northeast Corner Of The Basement

south.description: To the south lies The Southeast Corner Of The Basement.

west.description: You see athletes warming up and stretching.

12016.description:
A tall turning post of painted stone marks this corner of the sunken
yard, and around it the chariot track swings in a tight curve, rutted
deep by wheels and churned by hooves. The outer wall here is scarred and
splintered where chariots have taken the bend too fast. High above, the
galleries lean over the yard, and the sky shows grey between their
eaves. The track runs south toward the stables and west along the yard.

212017.name: The Southeast Corner Of The Basement

north.description: To the north lies The Northeast Corner Of The Basement.

west.description: To the west lies The Southwest Corner Of The Basement.

212017.description:
Here the warehouse's upper floor juts out over the corner of the yard,
roofing it with heavy beams, and beneath them the chariot teams are
stabled. Stalls of rough planking line the walls, and harness hangs from
pegs in tangles of leather and brass. The air is warm and thick with the
smells of horse, straw and liniment. The yard opens north along the
track and west toward the practice ground.

12018.name: The River Dock Entrance To The Warehouse

extra_descs.statue porter bronze plinth:
The porter is cast mid-stride, his back bent under a great sack and his
face set in grim patience. Letters on the plinth read: THIS PORT WAS
CARRIED HERE ON BACKS LIKE MINE.

12018.description:
Great double doors stand open in the warehouse wall here, wide enough
for two carts to pass, and a hoisting beam juts out above them with a
block and tackle swaying in the wind. The cobbles are grooved by iron-
shod wheels and dusted with chaff from cargo hauled up off the river
dock to the south. East, a rope rail marks where carters wait their turn
at the customs cage, and the sharp tang of vinegar and lye drifts from
the first-aid station to the west. Above the doors stands a weathered
bronze statue of a porter bowed beneath a sack.

east.description: The lines are very long and people look impatient.

south.description: A road lies in that direction.

west.description: An acrid, almost medicinal smell is coming from that direction.

12019.name: On The Canal By The Warehouse Dock
12019.description:
A broad stone quay runs beside the canal here, its edge lined with iron
bollards and fat rope fenders where barges tie up to unload. The great
stone bulk of the warehouse rises over the dock, and its wide river
doors stand open to the north. Wooden cranes lean out over the green
water, and the paving is stained with tar, brine and spilled grain. The
canal flows on east toward the sea, and the towpath runs back west along
the water.

north.description: You can hear the roar of a large crowd of people coming from that direction.

east.description: To the east lies On The Canal.

west.description: The highway continues to the west.

12021.name: The Mayor's House

east.description: To the east, a well manicured path winds through the nobleman's estate.

12021.description:
The mayor's house is grand in a slightly anxious way, as if straining to
keep up with the Dock Master's mansion across the lane. Its hall is
floored in chequered marble and hung with tapestries of ships and sea
battles, and a long table gleams with silver beneath a chandelier of
coloured glass. The air smells of beeswax and lavender. The front door
leads east, back out into the Wealthy Neighborhood.

12022.name: The Northwest Corner Of The Warehouse
12022.description:
This end of the warehouse yard lies open to the sky, and the salt wind
gusts across cobbles strewn with straw and broken barrel staves. Timber
scaffolding clings to the high wall here, where masons have been
patching the stonework after the winter storms, and dried splashes of
mortar whiten the ground beneath it. The yard runs on south between
stacked cargo, and to the west a roofed bay offers shelter under heavy
beams.

south.description: The common seating area continues.

west.description: The seating gets much fancier and elegant in that direction.

12023.name: The Southwest Corner Of The Warehouse
12023.description:
Cargo waits here in the open yard in long rows, barrels of salt fish and
lamp oil lashed under tarred canvas against the weather. Chalked marks
on the canvas tell which ship brought each load and which merchant
claims it. The din of shouted orders and rumbling wheels rolls in from
the busy entrance to the south, while the yard stretches on north toward
the far corner. The stones underfoot are dark with brine seeping from
the barrels.

north.description: The common seating area continues.

south.description: You see hundreds, perhaps thousands of people.

12024.name: East Entrance To Warehouse
12024.description:
A tall archway pierces the warehouse wall here, opening onto North Main
Street to the east. Just inside the arch the cobbles widen into a
crowded entrance court where wagons are unloaded and their cargo
tallied. South, the iron bars of the bonded area wall off goods held for
the customs house, and north the open yard runs on between stacked
bales. Above the arch a carved anchor and the faded words PORT HALYON
WAREHOUSE are cut into the keystone.

north.description: You see rows upon rows of dilapidated wooden bleachers.

east.description: Nero Drive lies in that direction.

south.description: There are VERY long lines standing outside the ticket booth.

12025.name: The Bonded Area

north.description: You see hundreds, if not thousands of people.

west.description: You see hundreds, if not thousands of people.

12025.description:
Behind a tall fence of iron bars, cargo held for the customs house waits
in sealed bales and crates, each tagged with a lead seal and a number.
Caged lamps hang from the beams and throw a mesh of shadow across the
swept floor. A clerk's counter closes the only gap in the bars, a heavy
cashbox bolted beneath it. Passages lead north toward the busy entrance
hall and west to the river dock doors.

212026.name: On The Canal

east.description: To the east lies On The Canal.

west.description: To the west lies On The Canal By The Warehouse Dock.

212026.description:
Your boat rocks on the green water of the canal, hemmed in by walls of
dressed stone higher than your head. Westward the channel widens beside
the warehouse dock, and the great stone bulk of the warehouse looms over
it. Eastward the canal runs straight toward the sea, and already the air
tastes of salt. Chaff and straw from the loading bays drift in a yellow
skin along the walls.

12027.name: The Wealthy Neighborhood

north.description: You see a paved road in the distance.

east.description: The path leads east through the estate.

south.description: You see an incredible house off in the distance.

west.description: Off through the trees, you see a small, plain hut.

12027.description:
A gravelled lane winds between clipped hedges and iron railings here,
past lawns so green they seem to have been painted. Through gates of
wrought iron you glimpse gardens of roses, fountains and fig trees. To
the south rises the great house of the Dock Master, its marble face
blazing white, and to the west the mayor's house stands behind a row of
cypresses. The lane leads north to River Avenue and east to South Main
Street.

12028.name: The Dock Master's House
12028.description:
The area opens in a house, the size and splendor of which almost defies
the imagination. The floor is done with hand crafted marble tile with
silver and jeweled inlays. The light coming through the exquisitely
crafted stained glass windows bathes the room in splendor and the
furniture looks as though it was made by master craftsmen from all over
the empire. A path through the estate is north of here. The walls are
rough- hewn and cold to the touch. The air is still and musty.

north.description: You see a well manicured path that winds through the estate.

12029.name: The North Gate
12029.description:
The great North Gate of Port Halyon stands shut and barred, its iron-
bound doors set between two squat towers of salt-grey stone. A heavy
beam rests across them in iron brackets, and the paving before the gate
is caked with dried mud carried in long ago from the road beyond. Arrow
slits look out from the towers over the countryside, and an empty
brazier stand rusts beside the guard post. Main Street leads back south
into the town, where the smell of the bakery hangs on the air.

south.description: Nero Drive continues in that direction.

12030.name: Main Street

north.description: To the north, you can see a gate leading out of the city.

south.description: Nero Drive continues in that direction.

west.description: You see the bakery of Rome.

12030.description:
The smell of fresh bread spills from the open door of the Bakery to the
west, warm and heavy enough to make your stomach growl. Main Street runs
north to the great North Gate, whose iron-bound doors stay shut and
barred against the road beyond. South, the street descends toward the
busy heart of the port. Flour dust whitens the doorstep and the gutter
beside it.

12031.name: North Main Street
12031.description:
North Main Street climbs here between tall merchant houses whose carved
balconies lean out over the paving, hung with pots of herbs and lines of
washing. The flagstones are polished by countless feet and cartwheels,
and the street rings with the cries of hawkers and the creak of signs.
It rises north toward Main Street and the North Gate, and falls away
south to the crossing where Wharf Avenue meets the road. West, a tall
archway opens into the great stone warehouse.

north.description: Nero drive continues in that direction.

south.description: It looks like the town square.

west.description: You see the an opulent estate.

12032.name: The North Main Street Intersection

north.description: Nero Drive heads in the direction of the northern gate.

east.description: Nero Drive heads in the direction of the south gate.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Street Bridge.

12032.description:
Wharf Avenue branches off east here toward the quays, and the smell of
fish, tar and wet rope rides along it on the wind. North Main Street
climbs away north between tall merchant houses with carved balconies. To
the south the road rises onto the stone hump of the Main Street Bridge.
Beyond the rooftops the long arches of the old aqueduct stride across
the skyline.

212033.name: The Main Street Bridge

north.description: To the north lies The North Main Street Intersection.

south.description: To the south lies The South Main Street Intersection.

212033.description:
The Main Street Bridge carries the road across the river on three broad
arches of weathered grey stone. Below, the brown water swirls around the
piers and leaves a ragged line of weed and froth on each cutwater. The
parapets are carved with leaping fish, worn almost smooth by wind and
idle hands. The road runs north to the busier crossing by Wharf Avenue
and south to the junction with River Avenue.

12034.name: South Main Street

north.description: Nero Drive leads in that direction.

east.description: To the east lies The Mage's Shop.

south.description: You see many people entering and leaving the city through a large gate in the walls protecting the city.

west.description: It looks like a nobleman's estate.  We are talking RICH nobleman's estate.

12034.description:
South Main Street runs broad and busy here between tall houses of
whitewashed stone, their shutters painted the blue of the harbour. A
narrow shopfront to the east is hung with bunches of dried herbs and a
sign of a silver crescent moon, where the Mage's Shop does its trade.
West, a gravelled lane turns off into the Wealthy Neighborhood. The
street runs north to the intersection with River Avenue and south to the
South Gate.

12035.name: The South Gate
12035.description:
The South Gate is a pair of tall bronze doors, green with age and salt,
closed and locked between towers of weathered stone. Through the grille
set in one leaf you can see a worn road leading away from the port into
low, scrubby hills. South Main Street runs north from here into the
town. A small shop crouches against the wall to the east, and a thin
pink mist curls out from under its door with a smell of sulphur and
singed hair.

north.description: Nero Drive leads towards the center of town.

east.description: A small store, from which an occasional detonation can be heard, lies off in that direction.  It appears to be surrounded by a rolling pink mist.

12036.name: The Dock Master's Private Office

extra_descs.chart coast pins map:
The chart shows the coast from the river mouth to the open sea, the safe
channels inked in blue and the reefs in red. One pin marks a ship many
days overdue, and beside it someone has written a single word: STORM.

12036.description:
The dock master's private office is richly furnished with goods brought
in from every port on the Sea of Storms: thick carpets, lamps of
coloured glass, and a massive carved desk heaped with manifests, harbour
dues and tide tables. A great chart of the coast covers one wall, stuck
with pins marking every ship expected in port. Potted plants and cut
flowers crowd the windowsill and every shelf, filling the room with a
green scent. French doors open east onto the waiting room, and a wooden
door leads south to the Council Room.

east.description: Through the door, you see a waiting room.

south.description: The south door leads directly to the senate chambers.

12037.name: The Council Room

north.description: The door is made of thick walnut.

east.description: The door leads to the foyer.

south.description: A passage leads to The House Of Commons

12037.description:
The council of Port Halyon meets in this tall room around a great
horseshoe table of polished oak, with a carved chair at its head for the
Dock Master and lesser chairs along its arms. On the wall hangs a vast
painted map of the harbour and the coast, its shipping lanes picked out
in gold leaf. A wooden door to the north leads to the Dock Master's
private office, a bronze door opens east into the entrance foyer, and
tall double doors lead south.

12038.name: The Committee Meeting Room

north.description: You see that the doublehung door leads to the senate chambers.

12038.description:
This smaller chamber is where the real business of the council gets
done, around a round table scarred with the rings of countless wine
cups. A slate board on one wall still bears the ghosts of chalked
figures, half wiped away: tonnages, tariffs, the names of ships. The
chairs are mismatched and comfortable, and a sideboard holds a row of
empty decanters. The tall double doors to the north lead back into the
Council Room.

12039.name: Wharf Avenue
12039.description:
Wharf Avenue runs wide and straight here, its paving grooved by heavy
carts bound for the quays. Ship's chandlers, rope-walks and sailmakers'
lofts line the way, their signs creaking in the salt wind, and the smell
of tar and fish grows stronger with every step. Above the rooftops the
long arches of the old aqueduct stride across the skyline. The avenue
carries on east toward the quays and the East Gate, and back west to the
crowded crossing with North Main Street.

east.description: Clay Avenue continues in that direction.

west.description: There are large crowds of people in that direction.

12042.name: The Mage's Shop
12042.description:
This is the mage's shop. Magical ointments, charms and potions are
sitting on shelves and behind a glass counter. There is a dense neon
blue fog hugging the floor here, making it impossible to see below your
knees. You suddenly hear mutterings coming from the back room, possibly
from...
KKKKKAAAAAABBBBOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!!!!!!
The area is deafened by the noise from a tremendous explosion and the
concussion from the blast staggers you! The shopkeeper seems to pay no
heed to this. The door to the back room opens and an older man, wearing
a pointed hat, whose face is smudged with soot sticks his head out. 'Is
everyone alright? Sorry about that. I was testing a new spell. I'll try
to give advance notice next time.', he says. The door then closes. The
air is still and musty. The walls are rough-hewn and cold to the touch.

east.description: The door is reinforced with steel and looks VERY sturdy.  Considering the 'test' that you just witnessed, you are glad that it stands between you and whatever is going on in the back room.

west.description: You see the south gate through the door.

12043.name: The Waiting Room
12043.description:
Long benches of polished oak line the walls of this tall chamber, where
petitioners wait their turn to see the dock master. A clerk's high desk
stands by the door with an appointment book chained to it and a brass
bell on a bracket above. Portraits of past dock masters, stern men and
women in sea coats, gaze down from the panelling. A door to the west
leads to the dock master's private office, another opens east into the
Office Of The Court Clerk, and a hallway runs south to the foyer.

east.description: There is a sign on the door that says:  MUNICIPAL COURT OF ROME.  It appears  to be open.

south.description: The foyer is directly to the south.

west.description: There is a large door to the west.

12044.name: The Entrance Foyer
12044.description:
The entrance foyer of the Capitol is a lofty hall under a painted dome,
where ships in full sail chase one another around a great compass rose.
The marble floor rings under every footstep, and benches for messengers
stand along the walls beneath tall lamps. A heavy bronze door to the
west leads into the Council Room, and a hallway runs north to the
waiting room. Broad marble stairs sweep down and out of the building to
the street.

north.description: You see a hallway leading north to what looks like a waiting room.

west.description: There is a large door to the west that blocks your path.

down.description: You see a stairway leading out of the building.

12045.name: Outside The Capitol
12045.description:
The area opens on white marble steps that lead up and into the Capitol
Building. There are several statues, none of any real significance, at
the entrance to the building. The main entrance to the building is at
the top of the steps. Vendors and pedestrians bustle past. The
cobblestones are worn smooth by countless feet.

up.description: The steps lead into the Capitol Building.

down.description: The steps terminate onto Clay Avenue.

12046.name: Wharf Avenue
12046.description:
This area is a wide, heavily traveled road that runs east and west
through the heart of the city. There are marble steps leading up. To the
south, off in the distance, Visible is a large stone structure and a
mountain that is partially obscured by the haze. There is a general
store to the north. The sounds of city life echo around. The smell of
smoke and humanity hangs in the air.

north.description: The general store lies in that direction.

east.description: There is what appears to be a large gate in that direction.

west.description: Clay Avenue continues.

up.description: There are some white marble steps leading up.

212047.name: On The Canal

east.description: To the east lies On The Canal.

west.description: To the west lies On The Canal.

212047.description:
Midway along its length the canal passes beneath a low timber
footbridge, and you must duck as your boat slides through its shadow.
Green weed hangs from the stone walls to the waterline, and the smell of
the tide grows stronger with every stroke. The water runs on east toward
the ocean side docks and back west toward the warehouse. Overhead, the
wheels of a cart rumble across the planks of the bridge.

12049.name: Altoor's Workshop
12049.description:
Altoor's Workshop is a cluttered, smoke-stained den behind the Mage's
Shop. Workbenches along the walls are crowded with beakers, coiled glass
tubes and crucibles, and the air reeks of sulphur, scorched wool and
something like burning tar. In the middle of the floor a circle of
chalked runes is blackened by fire, and a heap of grey cinders inside it
looks uncomfortably as if it was once a person. The only way out is the
steel-bound door west into the shop.

west.description: There is a door, reinforced with steel, in that direction.

12050.name: The Office Of The Court Clerk

extra_descs.seal anchor rope:
The seal is carved in dark oak and gilded: an anchor with a rope wound
about its shank, ringed by the words BY TIDE AND TALLY. The gilt is worn
away where nervous hands have touched it for luck.

12050.description:
The Office Of The Court Clerk doubles as the harbour court, where
quarrels over cargo, wages and dues are settled. The clerk's desk sits
below a raised bench, with a railed witness stand beside it and rows of
plain benches facing them both. Behind the bench hangs the seal of the
harbour council, an anchor wound about with rope. A door to the east
leads to the Mayor's Office, the Records Room lies to the south, and the
waiting room is back to the west.

east.description: The door might lead into the judge's private chambers.

south.description: The holding cells lie in that direction.

west.description: The waiting room lies in that direction.

12051.name: The East Gate Of Port Halyon
12051.description:
Two tall towers rise from the city wall here, crowned with watch
platforms that look out over the harbour and the docks. Between them a
heavy timber gate bound with iron closes the archway, opening east onto
the covered loading dock by the canal. The paving is crusted with salt
and strewn with straw blown in from the quays. Wharf Avenue leads back
west into the heart of the port.

east.description: The clay road heads eastwards.

west.description: The clay street leads into the city.

212052.name: On The Canal

east.description: To the east lies On The Canal By The Ocean Side Unloading Dock.

west.description: To the west lies On The Canal.

212052.description:
The canal broadens as it nears the sea, and its walls fall back to low
quays of tarred timber. Your boat begins to lift and settle on the first
long breaths of swell rolling in from open water. East of here the canal
mouth bristles with the cranes and hoists of the unloading dock.
Westward the channel narrows again between high stone walls.

12054.name: On The Canal By The Ocean Side Unloading Dock

north.description: To the north lies On the Canal Loading Dock.

east.description: To the east lies Along The Shoreline.

south.description: To the south lies Port Halyon.

west.description: To the west lies On The Canal.

12054.description:
The canal spills out here into the harbour, and the chop slaps hard
against the pilings of the unloading dock. A great wooden crane leans
out over the water, its hook swinging on a chain as thick as your wrist.
North of your boat a covered loading dock opens onto the quay, the
shoreline runs away east, and the broad harbour of Port Halyon spreads
to the south. The canal leads back west into the town.

12055.name: Mayor's Office

west.description: The courtroom lies in that direction.

12055.description:
The mayor's office is a comfortable, cluttered room panelled in honey-
coloured wood, with a broad desk heaped with petitions, a pair of
leather armchairs and a cabinet of rolled maps. A tall window of thick
green glass lets in a watery light and the distant sounds of the
harbour. Portraits of former mayors line the walls, each in a gilded
frame and each looking more pleased with himself than the last. A door
to the west leads back into the court clerk's office.

212056.name: River Avenue

east.description: To the east lies River Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies The Weapons Shop.

west.description: To the west lies The West Gate.

212056.description:
River Avenue begins its run along the riverbank here, a broad street of
cracked flagstones with a low wall on the water side. A painted sign of
crossed swords hangs over a stout door to the south, where the Weapons
Shop does its trade. The West Gate stands at the street's end to the
west, sand drifting in beneath its arch. Eastward the avenue follows the
river toward the heart of the port.

212057.name: River Avenue

east.description: To the east lies River Avenue.

west.description: To the west lies River Avenue.

212057.description:
Here the avenue runs close beside the river, and the smell of wet mud
and weed rises over the embankment wall. Iron mooring rings are set into
the wall at intervals, crusted with rust except where ropes have rubbed
them bright. Across the brown water stand the backs of warehouses, their
loading doors shut. The street carries on east toward Main Street and
west toward the desert gate.

12026.name: River Avenue

east.description: The road leads off to the east.

south.description: It looks like a Nobleman's estate.  We are talking RICH nobleman's estate.

west.description: To the west lies River Avenue.

12026.description:
The avenue widens before it meets Main Street, and the houses on its
southern side grow taller and better kept. A gravelled lane leads south
between iron railings into the Wealthy Neighborhood, where clipped
hedges hide the gardens from the street. On the river side a stone horse
trough stands half full of green water. The cobbles run on east to the
crossing with Main Street and back west along the river.

12033.name: The South Main Street Intersection

north.description: To the north lies The Main Street Bridge.

south.description: Nero Drive continues toward the South Gate.

west.description: A paved road runs west through the city.

12033.description:
River Avenue ends here against Main Street, and a weathered milestone at
the corner gives the distance to Garathorm in worn figures. To the north
the street climbs onto the Main Street Bridge, its stone parapets white
with salt and droppings. South Main Street runs on south between
shuttered shops, and River Avenue leads away west along the water. The
paving is grooved by cartwheels and dark with spilled fish brine.

extra_descs.milestone stone:
The milestone bears the name of Garathorm cut in tall, old-fashioned
letters, with a number of leagues beneath it. Weather and the hands of
travellers have worn the figures so smooth that the distance could be
almost anything.

12060.name: The Records Room

north.description: The courtroom lies to the north.

east.description: To the east lies The Records Room.

12060.description:
Shelves of dark wood rise from floor to ceiling in this long room,
crammed with bound ledgers whose spines are lettered by year: harbour
dues, court judgements, deeds of sale and the manifests of every ship
that has unloaded at Port Halyon. A long table runs down the middle,
with high stools and lamps set inside glass chimneys to guard the paper.
The air is dry and smells of dust and old ink. The court clerk's office
lies north, and a second records room opens east.

212061.name: The Records Room

west.description: To the west lies The Records Room.

212061.description:
This inner records room holds the oldest papers in the port, and it
shows: the shelves sag under scrolls in cracked leather cases and
bundles of brittle parchment tied with faded ribbon. A great iron chest
stands against the end wall, triple-locked, and above it hangs a framed
chart of the coast as it was drawn long ago, with sea monsters coiled in
its margins. Dust lies thick, broken only by a narrow trail of
footprints. The only way out is west.

extra_descs.chart map coast monsters:
The old chart shows Port Halyon as a cluster of huts beside a river
mouth. Far out to sea, among the drawn monsters, a ring of black pillars
is labelled in faded red ink: HERE THE SEA GOES DOWN.

12062.name: The Bakery
12062.description:
Warm, sweet air fills the bakery of Port Halyon, heavy with the smell of
fresh loaves, honey cakes and hard ship's biscuit. A great brick oven
glows behind the counter, and long wooden paddles hang on pegs beside
its iron door. Flour dusts every surface, from the scrubbed shelves to
the beams overhead. The only door leads east onto Main Street.

east.description: The cobblestones lead to Nero Drive

12063.name: The General Store
12063.description:
This is the busiest general store on the waterfront, and its shelves sag
under everything a sailor or traveller might need: coils of rope,
lanterns and lamp oil, tinderboxes, oilskin coats and casks of hard
biscuit. Nets and buckets hang from hooks in the low ceiling, and a long
counter scarred by years of trade runs the length of the room. The smell
of tar and soap mixes in the close air. The door opens south onto Wharf
Avenue.

south.description: Clay Avenue lies in that direction.

12064.name: On the Canal Loading Dock

south.description: To the south lies On The Canal By The Ocean Side Unloading Dock.

west.description: The cobblestones lead to The East Gate Of Rome

12064.description:
A long roof of tarred planks covers this loading dock, and the gloom
beneath it smells of hemp, pitch and bilge water. Pegs along the walls
hold coils of hawser, and a chalked board lists the hours of the tides.
A heavy gate in the west wall opens onto the East Gate of Port Halyon.
Northward the planking runs out into daylight along the Dock of Port
Halyon, and to the south it ends at the lip of the canal.

12057.name: The Dock Of Port Halyon

north.description: To the north lies The Dock Of Port Halyon.

east.description: To the east lies Along The Shoreline.

south.description: To the south lies On the Canal Loading Dock.

12057.description:
The dock runs out over a hump of black rock here, and tufts of sea pink
and coarse grass cling in its cracks. Wind off the water snaps at your
clothes and carries the cries of gulls from the rooftops. Eastward, the
rock breaks into ledges above the shoreline, where small boats put out.
The dock continues north toward the ocean end, and the covered loading
dock lies south.

212066.name: The Dock Of Port Halyon

north.description: To the north lies End Of The Ocean Dock.

east.description: To the east lies Along The Shoreline.

south.description: To the south lies The Dock Of Port Halyon.

212066.description:
Broad planks, grey and split by sun and salt, carry the dock out over
the water on a forest of tarred piles. Iron bollards squat along the
edge, wound with frayed rope and speckled white with droppings. Through
the gaps between the boards you can see green water heaving beneath your
feet. The dock runs on north to its far end and back south toward the
town, and a boat can push off east into the shallows.

212067.name: End Of The Ocean Dock

east.description: To the east lies Along The Shoreline.

south.description: To the south lies The Dock Of Port Halyon.

212067.description:
The dock ends in a square platform of heavy beams, open on three sides
to wind and spray. A tall post at its corner carries an iron lantern
cage, black with soot, to guide boats home after dark. On the east side
a weed-slick landing stage meets the water, where the shoreline currents
tug at anything afloat. The planks lead back south toward the town.

extra_descs.lantern post cage notches:
The iron cage at the top of the post is big enough to hold a fire
basket, and its bars are crusted with soot and salt. Notches cut into
the post mark the heights of great tides, the highest of them level with
your chin.

12101.name: Port Harem

north.description: To the north lies Ocean Pier.

east.description: To the east lies Beachside Harem.

12101.description:
Port Harem is little more than a scatter of gaudy houses along a sandy
shore, their shutters painted crimson and gold and peeling in the salt
air. Coloured lanterns sway on poles along the sand, and the breeze
carries a cloying smell of perfume and spilled wine. Behind the houses
the dunes are tufted with spiky sea holly. The Ocean Pier stretches out
over the water to the north, and a path follows the beach east toward a
grander house on a rise.

12102.name: Beachside Harem

east.description: To the east lies Beach Road.

west.description: To the west lies Port Harem.

down.description: To the down lies Harem.

12102.description:
A grand old house sits on a sandy rise above the beach, its walls washed
pink and its windows screened with carved lattices. Broad steps lead
down through its garden to a lower door, from which drift soft music and
the scent of incense. Wind-bent palms rattle their fronds overhead. Port
Harem lies west along the shore, and Beach Road leads away east.

12103.name: Beach Road

east.description: To the east lies Beach Road.

west.description: To the west lies Beachside Harem.

12103.description:
Beach Road is a track of packed sand and crushed shells running along
the top of the shore. On one side the surf rolls in long and lazy over a
pale beach, and on the other dunes crowned with marram grass hide the
land beyond. Shells crunch under every step. The road runs east toward a
dark hill and west to the pink house on its rise.

12104.name: Harem

up.description: To the up lies Beachside Harem.

12104.description:
This sunken courtyard lies below the Beachside Harem, hidden from the
world by high walls of pink plaster faded almost white by the sun. A
long pool of blue tiles fills its centre, though its water is green and
still, and silk awnings that once shaded the cushioned benches hang in
rags from their poles. Jasmine has run wild over the walls, and its
sweet scent is heavy in the warm air. A flight of steps leads up to the
Beachside Harem.

12105.name: Beach Road

east.description: To the east lies Vice Hill.

west.description: To the west lies Beach Road.

12105.description:
The road turns its back on the sea here and heads east toward the dark
bulk of Vice Hill. Sand gives way to hard earth, and the grass along the
verges is brown and trampled. A weathered post leans beside the road,
its sign long since torn away. Behind you to the west the sound of the
surf fades.

12106.name: Creepy Road

east.description: To the east lies Creepy Road.

west.description: To the west lies Vice Hill.

12106.description:
Creepy Road earns its name quickly, for the hedges on either side are
dead and grey and their bare twigs knot together overhead like clutching
fingers. The sky shows through them only in dull scraps. No bird sings,
and your footsteps sound too loud on the hard earth. The road runs on
east and back west to Vice Hill.

12107.name: Creepy Road

east.description: To the east lies Creepy Road.

west.description: To the west lies Creepy Road.

12107.description:
Here the dead hedges give way to a sagging iron fence, its spikes capped
with the bleached skulls of small animals. Beyond it a field of grey
weeds stretches toward a tall, dark building with a single tower. A cold
wind moans through the railings. The road continues east toward the
building and west between the hedges.

12108.name: Creepy Road

east.description: To the east lies Entrance To The Building Of Fear.

west.description: To the west lies Creepy Road.

12108.description:
Creepy Road ends here before the Building of Fear, a tall house of
black-stained timber that leans over the road as though listening. Its
windows are dark, and its crooked tower leans the other way. Two carved
posts flank the path, each topped with a grinning wooden face. The door
stands open a crack to the east, and the road leads back west.

extra_descs.posts faces carved:
The faces on the posts are carved with wide, staring eyes and far too
many teeth. Rain has run black streaks from their eyes, so that they
seem to weep as they grin.

12109.name: Vice Hill

south.description: To the south lies Vice Hill.

up.description: To the up lies Vice Hill.

12109.description:
Here at the foot of Vice Hill the slope meets a lane of beaten earth,
and the dens of the hill begin. Gaudy lanterns of red and yellow paper
hang from a line strung between two leaning posts, and a smell of
spilled wine and cheap incense drifts on the air. A track of worn steps
climbs up the slope toward the busier heights of the hill. The lane runs
on south between thickets of gorse.

12110.name: Vice Hill

north.description: To the north lies Vice Hill.

south.description: To the south lies Vice Hill.

12110.description:
The lane winds along the lower slope of Vice Hill between shacks of
tarred driftwood, their doors painted with dice, cups and grinning faces
to show what is sold within. Most stand shuttered, but the smell of
smoke and stale beer clings to every plank. Broken crockery glints among
the gorse at the roadside, where the hill's customers have flung their
empties. North, the lane runs back toward the steps that climb the hill,
and south it reaches a crossroads.

12111.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

east.description: To the east lies Vice Hill.

12111.description:
The tunnel opens east onto the slopes of Vice Hill, and a grey wash of
daylight seeps in to show walls black and glistening with tar. Just
inside the mouth the floor is scored with long gouges, as if something
heavy had been dragged through. Northward the passage runs straight into
blackness. The smell of pitch is strong enough to make your eyes water.

12112.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies Vice Hill.

12112.description:
The tunnel bores into the flank of Vice Hill through a frame of massive
timbers, every one of them painted thick with black pitch. Daylight and
the smell of grass reach a few paces in from the hillside to the west,
then give up. Beyond them the walls glisten with tar that has run and
hardened in long, rippled curtains. The passage leads north into the
dark, and the air breathing out of it is warm and sharp with the reek of
pitch.

12113.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12113.description:
The tunnel bends a little here, and a niche in the wall holds a crude
clay figure of a hooded man, its face smeared black with tar. Old candle
wax has dribbled over its feet in pale, lumpy layers. The darkness seems
to press in from both ends of the passage. Past the niche the tunnel
goes on north and south.

12114.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12114.description:
Tar seeps from cracks in the rock here and creeps down the walls in slow
black beads, pooling wherever the floor dips. The pools have set hard
enough to hold footprints, dozens of them, all pressed into the pitch
and all heading north. Torch brackets of rusted iron are fixed to the
walls at intervals, their sockets choked with soot. The tunnel runs on
north and back south toward the hillside.

12115.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12115.description:
A rusted iron grate is set into the tunnel wall here, covering a vent no
wider than your fist. Through it drifts a faint, far-off sound like many
voices chanting together. Tar has oozed over the grate and set into
black icicles along its lower bars. The passage leads on to the north
and back to the south.

12116.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12116.description:
A wide niche has been hacked out of the wall here to hold an iron
cauldron, its belly cracked and its rim furred with layers of old pitch.
The rock above it is scorched black, and the smell of burnt tar is so
strong that your eyes water. Someone once kept a fire going here day and
night to keep the walls freshly coated. Spilled tar has set in
treacherous ridges across the floor, and the tunnel continues north and
south.

12117.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12117.description:
Water drips from the roof here, beading on the tar and creeping along
the walls in slow black rivulets. A shallow gutter cut in the floor
carries it away, and its gurgle echoes through the dark. The air is
cooler here and smells of wet stone as well as pitch. North and south,
the passage fades into darkness.

12118.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12118.description:
The rock gives way here to loose earth, and the roof is held up by
tarred props and crossbeams that groan softly under their load. Black
drips gather on the beams and fall now and then onto the floor, where
they have built little cones of pitch like a field of tiny cairns. The
air is close and warm, and every sound stops short against the walls.
The tunnel leads north deeper into the hill and south toward the way
out.

12119.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12119.description:
The tunnel runs straight and utterly dark here, the tarred walls
swallowing what little light you carry. Handprints are pressed into the
soft tar at shoulder height, as though others felt their way along here
blind. Some of the prints are very small. The tunnel runs on north and
south.

12120.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12120.description:
Iron rings are set into both walls here at the height of a man's wrists,
and the tar beneath each one is scuffed and gouged by the struggling of
many feet. Long smears run along the floor where something, or someone,
was dragged. The walls have been tarred so often that the hewn rock is
lost beneath a smooth black skin that gleams in what little light there
is. The passage goes on north and falls away south.

12121.name: Tarry Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Entrance To The Hall Of Hopelessness.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

12121.description:
Thick black tar seals the stone blocks of this tunnel, oozing from the
joints and hanging in sticky drips from the roof. The air is close and
warm, and the reek of pitch catches in your throat. A faint glow from
the archway to the north gives the only light, while southward the
tunnel runs on into blackness. Your boots stick and unstick from the
floor with every step.

12122.name: Tarry Tunnel

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies Entrance To The Hall Of Hopelessness.

12122.description:
The tunnel ends here against a wall of bare rock, scraped clean of tar
in a broad square as if to make a page. Into it someone has chiselled
words in tall, careful letters, now half filled with soot. A low doorway
to the west opens on the Entrance To The Hall Of Hopelessness, and a
chill draught flows out of it, carrying a smell of cold ashes. The only
other way is back south along the tarry passage.

extra_descs.words letters inscription wall:
The letters read: HERE YOU WILL BE ASKED ONCE. Beneath them, in a
smaller and shakier hand, someone has scratched: AND THEN AGAIN, AND
AGAIN.

12123.name: Vice Hill

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Road.

east.description: To the east lies Tarry Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies Tarry Tunnel.

up.description: To the up lies Through The Trees.

down.description: To the down lies Vice Hill.

12123.description:
Near the top of Vice Hill the scrub thins to bare rock and black, tar-
smeared earth. Tunnel mouths gape in the hillside to the east and the
west, their rims caulked with pitch like the seams of a ship. A rutted
track heads north as Tarry Road, a path climbs up into a dark stand of
trees, and the way down leads back to the crossroads. The whole hilltop
smells of hot tar.

12124.name: Tarry Road

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Road.

south.description: To the south lies Vice Hill.

12124.description:
Tarry Road is a rutted track of black earth, so soaked with spilled
pitch that it clings to your boots. Rusted barrel hoops and charred
staves are half buried in the verges, and the grass between them is
dead. A bitter smoke hangs low over the ground. The road runs north
between low hummocks and south to the crown of Vice Hill.

12125.name: Tarry Road

north.description: To the north lies Tarry Road.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Road.

12125.description:
The road passes a pit of bubbling black tar here, fenced off by a few
crooked stakes. Bubbles swell and burst on its surface with lazy pops,
each one releasing a puff of stinking smoke. Near the edge, the bleached
ribs of some large beast poke out of the tar. The track runs on north
and back south.

extra_descs.pit tar bones ribs:
The pit is perhaps ten paces across, and there is no telling how deep it
goes. A stake driven in at its edge has sunk until only its tip shows,
as though the pit were slowly swallowing it.

12126.name: Tarry Road

east.description: To the east lies Deserted Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies Tarry Road.

12126.description:
Tarry Road ends at a long, low building of tarred black planks, half
sunk into the hillside. Its door hangs open to the east, and beyond it a
bare corridor runs away into the dark. Thistles grow tall around the
walls, but nothing at all grows on the road. The track leads back south
toward Vice Hill.

12128.name: Vice Hill

north.description: To the north lies Vice Hill.

east.description: To the east lies Trail of Terror.

south.description: To the south lies Cliff Road.

west.description: To the west lies High Path.

up.description: To the up lies Trail of Terror.

12128.description:
Four ways meet at this crossroads on the shoulder of Vice Hill, marked
by a tall post of black wood carved with a single staring eye. East of
it a broad stair of stone climbs up onto the Trail of Terror, its steps
spattered with drippings of red wax. The High Path runs off west along
the ridge, the Cliff Road strikes south toward the sea cliffs, and the
lane leads back north among the dens. The wind up here is cold and
carries the smell of incense.

extra_descs.post eye carving:
The eye is carved deep and painted white, with a black pupil that seems
to follow you whichever way you turn. Scraps of parchment are nailed
beneath it, bearing prayers, curses and the names of the missing.

12129.name: High Path

east.description: To the east lies Vice Hill.

south.description: To the south lies High Path.

12129.description:
The High Path leaves the crossroads on Vice Hill and runs along the
spine of the ridge, a narrow street paved with slabs of grey slate.
Tall, thin houses lean together on either side, their upper floors
jutting out so far that the strip of sky above is no wider than a hand.
Iron lamp brackets shaped like grasping claws hang above the doors. The
path turns south along the ridge, and the crossroads lies back to the
east.

12130.name: Trail of Terror

south.description: To the south lies Trail of Terror.

west.description: To the west lies Vice Hill.

12130.description:
The Trail of Terror begins at the head of a stair from Vice Hill and
runs south along the hillside between high walls of soot-blackened
stone. Iron cages hang from brackets above the street, creaking in the
wind, empty but for a few rags snagged in their bars. Black candles burn
in niches along the walls, and their wax has run down the stone in long
tears. The stair leads back west to the crossroads.

12131.name: High Path

north.description: To the north lies High Path.

south.description: To the south lies High Path.

12131.description:
A gap between the houses here opens onto a sweeping view: the roofs of
Port Halyon spread out far below, and beyond them the grey expanse of
the Sea of Storms stretches to the horizon. A low parapet guards the
drop, its stones carved with the initials of lovers and the names of the
drowned. The slates of the street are slick with sea mist. The path
follows the ridge north and south.

12132.name: Trail of Terror

north.description: To the north lies Trail of Terror.

south.description: To the south lies Trail of Terror.

12132.description:
Masks are nailed to every door along this stretch of the trail, carved
from pale wood and painted with faces caught in the moment of screaming.
There are hundreds of them, so close together that the walls seem to
howl without a sound. The cobbles underfoot are worn into a shallow
trough down the middle, as if by countless processions. Southward the
trail goes on toward the temple, and northward it returns to the head of
the stair.

12133.name: High Path

north.description: To the north lies High Path.

south.description: To the south lies High Path.

12133.description:
The High Path narrows here to a stepped alley between blank walls that
shut out all but a thread of grey daylight. Doors are few and all of
them bolted, and the windows high above are fitted with iron grilles.
Pale crusts of wax are stuck to every tread, dripped from the candles of
some procession that passed this way. The alley runs on north and south.

12134.name: Trail of Terror

north.description: To the north lies Trail of Terror.

south.description: To the south lies Trail of Terror.

12134.description:
A gibbet of black oak stands over the trail here, its arm reaching out
across the street and its chain ending in an empty iron collar. Beneath
it a stone slab is carved with a long list of names, each followed by a
single word for what that person feared most. The smell of incense grows
heavier, drifting along the street from the south. Shuttered houses line
the trail as it runs on south and back north.

extra_descs.slab names list stone:
The list runs on and on: TOLAN, DROWNING. MERREN, THE DARK. ASCH, HER
FATHER. Some of the newest names have nothing carved after them yet.

12135.name: High Path

north.description: To the north lies High Path.

south.description: To the south lies High Path.

12135.description:
A little square opens on the High Path here around a well with a domed
stone cover, its iron lid locked fast with a chain. Lantern posts stand
at each corner of the square, their glass panes painted black so that
they give only a thin red glimmer. On the wall of one house a faded
mural shows a procession of hooded figures winding toward a temple on a
hill. From the square the path leads on north and south.

12136.name: Trail of Terror

north.description: To the north lies Trail of Terror.

south.description: To the south lies Trail of Terror.

12136.description:
The walls on either side of the trail are painted with eyes, thousands
of them, white and staring, from the gutters to the eaves. Whoever
painted them took care that wherever you stand, some of them look
straight at you. A dead tree grows through a crack in the paving, its
bare branches hung with little bundles of hair and bone tied up in red
thread. Under the low grey sky the trail continues north and slopes
south toward the temple doors.

12137.name: High Path

north.description: To the north lies High Path.

south.description: To the south lies Hall Of Wax.

12137.description:
The High Path ends at a low side door set deep in the wall of the Temple
of Terror, whose dark bulk rises above the last of the houses. The door
is narrow and plain, but a smell of warm tallow seeps from around its
frame, and the step before it is crusted with drips of wax. This is the
way the temple's servants come and go unseen. The door leads south into
the Hall Of Wax, and the path runs back north along the ridge.

12138.name: Trail of Terror

north.description: To the north lies Trail of Terror.

south.description: To the south lies Entrance To The Temple Of Terror.

12138.description:
The trail ends before the great door of the Temple of Terror, which
fills the south side of the street behind a portico of squat black
columns. The door is sheathed in iron and studded with nails whose heads
are shaped like screaming faces, and a heavy knocker in the shape of a
fist hangs at its centre. Smoke of incense seeps out around its edges,
sweet and choking. Back to the north the trail runs between its painted
walls.

12139.name: Vice Hill

east.description: To the east lies Creepy Road.

west.description: To the west lies Beach Road.

up.description: To the up lies Vice Hill.

down.description: To the down lies Vice Hill.

12139.description:
Vice Hill rises steep and stony here, its slopes choked with thorny
scrub and stunted, leaning trees. One path scrambles up toward the
summit, and another drops down the hillside into a fold of shadow.
Creepy Road runs off east between dead hedges, while Beach Road leads
back west toward the sea. A crooked signpost stands at the crossing, its
arms pointing every which way.

extra_descs.signpost sign post arms:
The signpost's arms have been turned and nailed back so many times that
none of them can be trusted. Someone has carved a grinning face into the
post, and someone else has tried to hack it out again.

12140.name: Cliff Road

north.description: To the north lies Vice Hill.

south.description: To the south lies Cliff Road.

12140.description:
The Cliff Road leaves the crossroads on Vice Hill and strikes out along
the brink of the sea cliffs, a ledge of bare grey rock hardly wide
enough for a cart. On one side the cliff rises in cracked and weathered
terraces; on the other it drops sheer to the surf boiling far below. The
wind tears at your cloak and fills your mouth with salt. The road runs
on south and back north to the hill.

12141.name: Cliff Road

north.description: To the north lies Cliff Road.

south.description: To the south lies Cliff Road.

12141.description:
A chain as thick as your thumb has been pinned to the rock face along
this stretch, giving travellers something to cling to where the ledge
narrows to a few feet. Its links are rusted orange except where hands
have gripped them bright. Far beneath, the sea surges into a cleft in
the cliff and booms like a drum. With the chain to guide you, the road
edges on north and south.

12142.name: Cliff Road

north.description: To the north lies Cliff Road.

south.description: To the south lies Cliff Road.

12142.description:
Here the road passes a shallow overhang in the cliff face, where
travellers have sheltered from the wind and left the black smudges of
old fires on the rock. Clumps of sea thrift cling to the ledges, nodding
pink heads in the gusts. Out over the water the horizon is lost in grey
haze. The ledge leads north toward Vice Hill and south to where the road
comes to an end.

12143.name: Cliff Road

north.description: To the north lies Cliff Road.

12143.description:
The Cliff Road comes to an abrupt end here, where a great slice of the
cliff has fallen into the sea and taken the road with it. The broken
edge is raw and pale, and a heap of stones has been piled at the brink
as a warning, topped with the bleached skull of a goat. Beyond the gap
the old roadway can be seen running on along the cliffs, out of reach.
There is nowhere to go but back north.

extra_descs.cairn stones skull warning:
The cairn is built from the stones of the fallen road. A line has been
scratched into the topmost stone: THE ROAD GOES ON, BUT NOT FOR YOU.

12145.name: Entrance To The Building Of Fear

east.description: To the east lies The Tapestry Room.

west.description: To the west lies Creepy Road.

12145.description:
The front hall of the Building of Fear is tall and narrow, panelled in
dark wood that has warped and split with damp. A single lamp burns with
a sickly green flame above the door, making the shadows twitch and jump.
A threadbare red runner leads east into a room hung with tapestries, and
the door behind you opens west onto Creepy Road. Somewhere deep in the
house a floorboard creaks.

12146.name: The Tapestry Room

east.description: To the east lies Trophy Room.

west.description: To the west lies Entrance To The Building Of Fear.

12146.description:
Huge tapestries cover every wall of this long room, faded to the colours
of dried blood and old bruises. They show scenes of terror: a ship
dragged under by a vast serpent, a city in flames, and a crowd fleeing
from something the weaver never finished. The eyes of the woven figures
seem to follow you as you cross the floor. Doorways lead east to a room
of trophies and west to the entrance hall.

extra_descs.tapestries tapestry weaving:
The largest tapestry shows a tall figure in a pale mask standing over a
kneeling crowd. Its face has been picked away thread by thread, as if
someone could not bear to look at it.

12147.name: Gargoyle Room

south.description: To the south lies Trophy Room.

12147.description:
Stone gargoyles crouch on pedestals all around this round, windowless
room, wings half spread and mouths gaping in silent howls. Their eyes
are chips of red glass that catch the light of a lamp hanging from the
ceiling. The air is cold, and each time you look away you could swear
one of them has shifted. The only door leads back south to the trophy
room.

12148.name: Trophy Room

north.description: To the north lies Gargoyle Room.

east.description: To the east lies Wailing Tower.

south.description: To the south lies Dressing Room.
